historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~0%) diverges from revenue (+4%) and EPS (+16-24%) by far more than 30%: Loblaw returns essentially all earnings via buybacks (C$1.1-1.9bn/yr) and dividends, so book value does not compound and is not a usable growth proxy. EPS CAGRs are flattered by the FY2020 COVID base, buybacks (count -4%/yr) and FY2025's 53rd week. Revenue CAGR is the anchor; EPS growth above it is buyback + modest margin, which the flat-count owner-FCF model expresses through margin and the SBC/buyback convention, not through share shrinkage.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (treatment B: CSV FCF less lease principal+interest less SBC, total company): FY2019 1,513; FY2020 2,591; FY2021 2,226; FY2022 1,788; FY2023 2,069; FY2024 2,034; FY2025 2,425 (continuing-only 2,148). Lease cash has grown from 2.49% of revenue (FY2019) to 2.66% (FY2025), faster than revenue, so the lease-adjusted FCF CAGR (5yr -1.3%) sits below the reported-FCF CAGR (+0.8%) - a growing share of OCF is pre-committed to rent. FY2020 is a COVID working-capital peak; FY2022-FY2025 shows the underlying ~2.0-2.4bn range. Revenue CAGRs use FY2025 continuing revenue against prior-year totals that included PC Financial (~C$1.2-1.4bn), so they understate retail growth by ~0.5pp.

scenario_narratives.base: Loblaw keeps doing what it has done since 2019: ~3.5% revenue growth from ~75 net new (mostly hard-discount and Shoppers) stores, food inflation around 2%, pharmacy scope-of-practice services and C$4.6bn e-commerce; adjusted EBITDA margin creeps from 11.3% to 11.8% as the automated DCs, Loblaw Advance retail media and discount mix deliver management's 'earnings faster than sales'; C$2.4bn/yr gross capex glides to ~3.1% of sales; leases stay ~2.65% of sales. Owner FCF (after rent, growth capex and tax, before interest) rises from ~C$2.2bn to ~C$3.4bn by FY2035; the PC Financial sale is already closed and the EQB stake sits in the bridge at market. Terminal value is capped at 18x owner FCF - the current ~33x is not carried forward.
scenario_narratives.bull: Discount-format share gains and the pharmacy/healthcare profit pool (clinics, prescribing, Connected Healthcare) compound at 4-4.5% while PC Optimum data, Loblaw Advance and DC automation lift adjusted EBITDA margin to 12.5%; capex normalises to 3.0% of sales once the 2030 C$10bn programme passes its peak; the Code of Conduct proves toothless and food-pricing politics fade. Exit at 20x owner FCF with 3% terminal growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: Grocery pricing becomes a durable political target: the Grocery Code of Conduct, Competition Bureau scrutiny and bread-price-fixing litigation force visible price investment while Walmart Canada, Costco and Empire's discount banners take share; immigration-driven population growth slows so revenue grows ~2%; adjusted EBITDA margin compresses 80bp to 10.5%; lease cost drifts to 2.8% of sales on rent escalation and new-store leases; capex stays at 3.3% to defend the network. The loss of PC Financial's diversifying earnings leaves a pure Canadian retailer valued at 15x owner FCF with 2% terminal growth. This is a margin-compression case, not a solvency case - net debt ex leases is ~0.7x EBITDA.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House owner-FCF basis: adjusted EBITDA plus SBC, less SBC (charged once), less the full lease cash cost (principal and interest, treatment B), less D&A ex right-of-use for a 26% cash tax on unlevered EBIT, plus D&A, less gross capex (disposals not netted), less 5% of revenue growth for working capital. Lease liabilities are therefore excluded from net debt; the EQB stake is a bridge asset with its income excluded from the flows; NCI is capitalised in the bridge. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon and a scenario-specific FCF cap (15/18/20x) and is floored at zero. Share count is held flat because Loblaw is a funded repurchaser. All values in CAD, same currency as the TSX quote.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is ~60% of EV: the 18x owner-FCF cap versus the ~33x the market pays today is the whole gap between the model and the price
Lease cost held at 2.65% of sales; Choice Properties (controlled by George Weston) is the landlord for C$836m/yr of rent, so rent escalation is a related-party decision
Cash tax at 26% on unlevered EBIT ignores the interest shield on C$5.9bn of debt (handled in WACC); a lower Canadian corporate rate would add ~C$1.5/share
EQB stake marked at a listed price (C$119.33 on 2026-10-09); a rate-sensitive challenger bank, it moved 10% between close and valuation date
Regulatory intervention in grocery pricing (Code of Conduct, Competition Bureau) is the bear axis; the model prices it via scenario weights, not a WACC premium
Majority control by George Weston Limited: no takeover premium is possible and related-party leases/dividends to Weston (C$290m+/yr) are set by the controller

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 54.44-69.59; EQB.TO price from the same endpoint for the bridge
data_sources.financials: L.TO_Metrics.csv (metrics_normalized, CAD millions, FY2014-FY2025 plus quarters to Q2-2026); FY2025 Annual Report (FCF table s.6.1, total debt s.6.2, cash flow statement, notes 6, 22, 25, 27); Q2-2026 Quarterly Report (MD&A s.1 PC Financial close, s.10 Outlook, balance sheet, cash flow statement, notes 4, 6, 9)
data_sources.qualitative: L.TO_Analysis.json (bull/bear cases, growth drivers, recent developments incl. 1 Jul 2026 EQB close and Sep 2026 store-opening raise)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 continuing-operations (Retail) revenue, 53 weeks ended 3 Jan 2026; PC Financial is in discontinued operations. The 53rd week (~C$1.2bn) is absorbed by the low year-1 growth rate rather than by restating the base.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,155.6m issued and outstanding net of shares held in trust at 20 Jun 2026 (Q2-2026 note 9) plus ~10.0m dilutive equity-award and other-liability effect (Q2-2026 diluted 1,169.5m vs basic 1,159.6m weighted average). Post 4-for-1 split (Aug 2025). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, buybacks (C$1.875bn FY2025, C$1.2bn H1-2026) are the funded mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral here.
inputs.net_debt_note: Treatment (B) for leases: lease liabilities (C$10,666m at 20 Jun 2026) are EXCLUDED from debt because the full lease cash cost is charged inside the flows. total_debt = long term debt 5,912 (Q2-2026 BS; no short term debt, bank indebtedness or current LTD at 20 Jun 2026) + 315 'certain other liabilities' the company itself counts as debt (failed sale-leaseback financial liabilities, FY2025 MD&A 6.2). cash = 998 cash + 14 short term investments (ex held-for-sale) + 235 cash consideration + 36 commodity-tax receivable received on the 1 Jul 2026 PC Financial close (Q2-2026 MD&A). PC Bank's own held-for-sale cash/ST investments (C$742m) left with the bank; press reports put total cash received incl. a pre-close excess-capital distribution at ~C$625m, which would add ~C$0.3/share and is not taken.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Continuing-operations OCF 5,945 less continuing capital investments 2,030 (FY2025 annual report, Free Cash Flow table, s.6.1). The Metrics.csv FY2025 FreeCashFlow of 4,202 is total-company (includes PC Financial OCF 319 and capex 32) and pre-lease. The company's own FCF definition (OCF - capex - interest paid - lease payments net) gives 1,910 continuing; the house owner FCF is unlevered so interest paid on debt is not deducted here.
inputs.lease_cash_note: FY2025 'Lease payments, net' 1,698 = principal 1,255 + interest 453 (both on the cash flow statement) less 10 finance-lease receipts; all continuing. last_fcf = reported_fcf 3,915 - lease cash 1,698 - SBC 69 - interest income 0 = 2,148.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report note 25: equity-based compensation expense C$69m (2024: C$63m), recognised in operating income. No net-share-settlement tax line disclosed (shares are bought into trust for RSU/PSU settlement, C$69m FY2025, already inside buyback cash).
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received C$20m FY2025; net debt is positive so no interest-income strip (rule: strip only when net cash > 1x FCF base).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 common shares purchased and cancelled C$1,875m plus C$69m bought into trust and C$37m tax on repurchases; H1-2026 a further C$1,200m. Loblaw is a funded repurchaser, so the flat count is paid for.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Saturday closest to 31 December (FY2025 = 53 weeks ended 3 Jan 2026)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T20:00:00Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 54.44-69.59
inputs.wacc_rationale: CAD-denominated flows discounted at a CAD-built rate: 10y Government of Canada ~3.3%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta 0.75 for a defensive Canadian grocer/pharmacy -> cost of equity ~7.1%; after-tax cost of debt ~3.0% (FY2025 notes issued at 4.0% weighted, 26% tax); ex-lease debt ~8% of EV -> ~6.7%, rounded up to 7.0% to carry the lease-rent escalation risk that treatment (B) leaves in the flows at historical cost. Same WACC in all three scenarios; risk is in the driver paths (adaptations rule f).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (principal + interest, FY2025 C$1,698m net, 2.66% of revenue) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities are excluded from net debt; D&A for cash tax is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 2,692 continuing less ROU depreciation 1,141 less Shoppers/Lifemark acquired-intangible amortisation 149 that adjusted EBITDA already strips = 1,402, 2.19% of revenue). EBITDA margin path is adjusted EBITDA PLUS the SBC expense (7,156 + 69 = 7,225, 11.31%) so that sbc_pct_path charges SBC exactly once. Consistent with the company's own FCF definition and with 3116.T / MPG.NZ in this folder.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI charged once, in the bridge: FY2025 NCI share of earnings C$71m (FY2024 104, FY2023 87) capitalised at ~10x = -C$800m rather than the C$164m book value; flows are left whole-company. Associate interest (C$376m liability, franchisee equity in consolidated Shoppers stores) is not deducted: the associates' earnings share is already expensed above operating income.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 2: operating company, non-US, material leases, minority interest, non-operating asset). Loblaw is Canada's largest food and drug retailer; PC Financial (President's Choice Bank) was sold to EQB on 1 Jul 2026, so the bank is NOT valued as a deposit-taker inside this model - the retail flows are continuing-operations only and the consideration is in the bridge (cash) and equity_bridge (EQB stake, matching-asset rule: EQB's equity-accounted income is excluded from the flows). Choice Properties was deconsolidated in late 2018 and FY2014-2017 debt includes it; FY2014 is the Shoppers Drug Mart transition year; all historical trend work here starts from FY2019 (first IFRS 16 year) on the lease-adjusted owner-FCF series. Per-share history in the CSV is already post 4-for-1 split. Working capital: inventories 6,562 + receivables 1,489 exceed trade payables 7,233 by ~C$0.8bn, so growth consumes cash modestly -> wc_capture -5% of the revenue change (FY2025 non-cash WC change -132, FY2024 +84). Cash tax: income taxes paid 1,002 on a lease-adjusted EBIT of ~4,056 = 24.7% cash rate; FY2025 continuing effective rate 29.3% was inflated by the PC Financial outside-basis deferred tax; Canadian statutory ~26.5% -> 26% flat on unlevered EBIT. Horizon 10 years: margins are near-mature but the capex programme (C$2.4bn/yr, ~75 stores/yr, automated DCs) needs the decade for D&A to catch up with capex. Price is a regular close, not after-hours.

base.growth_note: Y1 2.0% is ~4% underlying growth net of the FY2025 53rd week (H1-2026 continuing revenue +2.5%; Q2 food same-store +1.6%, drug +4.6%); then 3.5% (inflation ~2%, ~75 net new stores/yr, pharmacy services, e-commerce) decaying to 2.5% terminal.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA margin (post-IFRS 16): FY2023 11.2%, FY2024 11.1%, FY2025 11.31%. Guidance 'retail earnings faster than sales': +10bp/yr from discount-format mix, DC automation, Loblaw Advance retail media and pharmacy services, plateauing at 11.8% - grocery politics (Code of Conduct, Competition Bureau) cap how far margin can visibly expand.
base.lease_cost_note: FY2025 lease cash 2.66% of revenue (FY2019-24 range 2.32-2.63%); held flat - new stores add leases roughly in proportion to sales.
base.da_pct_note: D&A ex right-of-use depreciation and ex acquired-intangible amortisation: FY2025 2.19%. Rises toward capex as the C$2.4bn/yr programme (fixed assets 7,026 -> 7,717 in 12 months) depreciates.
base.capex_note: Gross capex guidance ~C$2.4bn for 2026 (3.65%); FY2023-25 3.2-3.6%. Disposal proceeds (C$262m FY2025) are NOT netted, matching the company's FCF definition. Glides to 3.1% as the DC-automation cycle completes; still above D&A (growth capex) in the terminal year.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.0%/2.5% is 22.8x FCF; capped at 18x - a mature defensive grocer, below the 20x house default for compounders. Current EV/owner-FCF is ~33x, so the model assumes multiple compression, not expansion.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the regulatory/political axis (Code of Conduct, Competition Bureau, affordability politics, a majority-controlled board with a C$500m price-fixing settlement in its history) is live and asymmetric for a company whose margin is the political variable; bull cut from 35% to 25% because its margin expansion requires the same regulators to stay quiet AND the retail-media/healthcare profit pools to scale, two independent things, in a saturated domestic market with one pilot US store. Base 50%: a steady, defensive, funded-buyback compounder.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
